title: OK if you don't mind the clean up
text:
OK if you don't mind the clean up. Fed up awhile ago with George Foreman grills. Awful to clean and the best one I had the paint melted off the back of it and smoked and ran if I cooked for more than a few minutes, and well, that was the best one I had.

I replaced it with a very heavy Hamilton Beach grill with temp control, removable plates that were also non stick and dishwasher safe. It has served me for a couple of years but like with many of these double grills, the food always seemed more steamed than grilled. It was also monstrously heavy and though pretty compact, you had to be real careful the heavy plates were secured when you moved it.

I saw a grill similar to this one in a catalog and thought I would look into what was out there. I was torn between this and the more expensive Zojirushi. Really could not decide. I guess it was the cover that won me over. And that the grill plate was immersible. The cover does come in handy if you don't want to splatter the place up and you don't mind a little steaming going on. I don't find it causes as much steaming as two sided grills - the cover is loose so it doesn't steam up as much as it could. The grill marks are definitely better, probably because of the higher heat and reduced steaming. I was not sure I would like the little griddle part but it is nice. I can make little potato wedges pretty quickly on it, usually faster than the meat, have to watch that. Put a couple of slices of bacon on it another time.

I am still in a learning curve with timing but hoping to nail a london broil soon. I am notorious for killing london broils on anything but an outdoor grill and so far have had two flops. Both going by recipe time or booklet time. Some day. Maybe I will get that perfect medium rare and not gray throughout.

Then there is the cleaning. Oh. Well, I have not tried to put the grill surface in the dishwasher yet. I don't care to wreck nonstick in the DW. I would put my HB's grill plates in once in a while but didn't want to run down the nonstick. So I have been soaping up in a sink and letting the suds sit for a bit and scrubbing with a George Foreman grill sponge. It does an adequate job. But often have to use a grout type brush to get in between in the slats. It still does not come out perfectly clean but I can usually take a soapy dishcloth and get the last spots while it drips on the counter. I dry it and pop it in the stand. The water tray is another tricky deal. You definitely don't want to put too much water in there, very difficult to get it to the sink or a coffee can or wherever you are going to dump it. It is best to transport it in the plastic base as close as possible to where you will be dumping. I sometimes dump it in the DW if there is room. Otherwise, it is really not difficult to wash in the sink. The lid is similar though I often stick that in the DW if I need room in my drainboard for other things.

It did a nice job on burgers and steaks. And of course the potato wedges were a nice surprise. Pork chops were not good but I think it was really a case of bad tough pork chops to begin with. Chicken I overcooked, which like London broil I tend to be challenged by. It is nice, a little more work to clean so as not something I want to use everyday but I can use it once or twice a week without be traumatized by the clean up.

UPDATE: I have put it in the dishwasher and was pleasantly surprised. I mean I put the grilling grate in there. I have a tiny, cruddy little apt dishwasher and it just fit but I put the socket end toward the door so it would not get too soaked and I have got to say it came out nice. It also rusted on the bottom. Such is putting anything metal in the dishwasher. I would certainly not put this any more often in the dw than I did my Hamilton Beach grill grates. But when you have the room, don't have the time or patience to deal with it in the sink, yeah, it is what I would call dishwasher safe.

UPDATE - the second trip through DW will be its last. It didn't get it clean and there was a nasty grease film on everything else in the DW. Won't do it again. The coating seems more worn than ever I have used it 5 times and twice tried to use DW. Backing it down to three stars because cleanup is practically impossible from what I see/have experienced at this point

features: Ribbed grilling surface to drain grease
Solid area to grill vegetables, pancakes or keeping grilled foods warm
description: Heart Smart¿ Indoor Grill. Cooking surface has a ribbed area to drain grease for low-fat grilling, Plus a solid area to grill vegetables, pancakes or keeping grilled foods warm. Virtually smokeless grilling - add water to interior water level markings. Dishwasher safe grill surface and drip tray. Non-stick 15" x 11" grilling surface. Glass cover and heat resistant handles.
